title: Two-Number Addition
requirement: Design an LD function that reads two REAL input variables, Input1 and Input2, calculates their sum, and writes the result to the output variable Result. The program shall correctly handle positive numbers, negative numbers, and decimal values.

title: Fahrenheit-to-Celsius Conversion
requirement: Design an LD function that reads the REAL input variable Fahrenheit, converts the input temperature to Celsius, and writes the result to the REAL output variable Celsius.

title: Average of Five Values
requirement: Design an LD program that reads five REAL input variables, Input1 through Input5, calculates their arithmetic mean, and writes the result to the REAL output variable Average. The program shall correctly handle positive values, negative values, zero, and decimal values.

title: Difference Between Two Dates
requirement: Design an LD function that reads two DATE input variables, Date1 and Date2, calculates the absolute difference between them in days, and writes the non-negative result to the UDINT output variable DaysDifference. The result shall be independent of the input order.

title: Multiplication of Two 2-by-2 Matrices
requirement: Design an LD program that reads eight DINT input variables representing two 2-by-2 matrices, MatrixA and MatrixB, calculates their matrix product MatrixC = MatrixA * MatrixB, and writes the four resulting elements to the DINT output variables C11, C12, C21, and C22. The elements of MatrixA are represented by A11, A12, A21, and A22, and the elements of MatrixB are represented by B11, B12, B21, and B22. Each input value shall be within the range from -1000 to 1000.

title: Linear Interpolation
requirement: Design an LD function that reads five REAL input variables, X1, Y1, X2, Y2, and X, and calculates the linearly interpolated value of Y at X. The result shall be written to the REAL output variable Y. X1 and X2 shall not be equal, and X shall lie within the closed interval defined by X1 and X2. The calculation shall be independent of the order of the two known points.

title: Point Inside a Circle
requirement: Design an LD function that reads the REAL coordinates of a point, PointX and PointY, the REAL coordinates of a circle center, CenterX and CenterY, and the REAL radius Radius. The program shall determine whether the point lies inside or on the boundary of the circle and write the result to the BOOL output variable IsInside. Radius shall be greater than 0.0.

title: Three-Phase Current Unbalance Calculation
requirement: Design an LD program that reads three positive REAL input variables, CurrentA, CurrentB, and CurrentC, representing the RMS currents of a three-phase load. The program shall calculate the average current and the current unbalance rate. The average current shall be written to the REAL output variable AverageCurrent. The unbalance rate shall be calculated as the maximum absolute deviation of the three phase currents from the average current, divided by the average current, and expressed as a percentage in the REAL output variable UnbalanceRate.

title: Three-Phase Active Power Calculation
requirement: Design an LD function that reads three REAL input variables, LineVoltage, LineCurrent, and PowerFactor, representing the line-to-line RMS voltage, line current, and power factor of a balanced three-phase load. The program shall calculate the active power in kilowatts and write the result to the REAL output variable ActivePower. LineVoltage and LineCurrent shall be non-negative, and PowerFactor shall be within the range from 0.0 to 1.0.

title: Liquid Volume in a Cylindrical Tank
requirement: Design an LD function that reads two REAL input variables, TankDiameter and LiquidLevel, representing the internal diameter of a vertical cylindrical tank and the current liquid level. The program shall calculate the liquid volume in cubic meters and write the result to the REAL output variable LiquidVolume. TankDiameter shall be greater than 0.0, and LiquidLevel shall be non-negative. Use 3.14159265 as the value of pi.

title: Determinant of a 3-by-3 Matrix
requirement: Design an LD function that reads nine DINT input variables representing a 3-by-3 matrix, calculates its determinant, and writes the result to the DINT output variable Determinant. The matrix elements are represented by A11 through A33, where the first index denotes the row and the second index denotes the column. Each input value shall be within the range from -100 to 100.

title: Quadratic Equation Solver
requirement: Design an LD function that reads three REAL input variables, CoefficientA, CoefficientB, and CoefficientC, representing the quadratic equation CoefficientA * x^2 + CoefficientB * x + CoefficientC = 0. CoefficientA shall not be equal to 0.0. The program shall calculate the real roots of the equation and write the number of distinct real roots to the DINT output variable RootCount. If the discriminant is greater than 0.0, RootCount shall be 2, Root1 shall be calculated as (-CoefficientB + SQRT(Discriminant)) / (2.0 * CoefficientA), and Root2 shall be calculated as (-CoefficientB - SQRT(Discriminant)) / (2.0 * CoefficientA). If the discriminant is equal to 0.0, RootCount shall be 1 and the repeated root shall be written to both Root1 and Root2. If the discriminant is less than 0.0, RootCount shall be 0 and both Root1 and Root2 shall be set to 0.0.

title: Two-Variable Linear Equation Solver
requirement: Design an LD function that reads six DINT input variables, A1, B1, C1, A2, B2, and C2, representing the system of linear equations A1 * x + B1 * y = C1 and A2 * x + B2 * y = C2. The program shall determine whether the system has a unique solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions. The DINT output variable SolutionType shall be set to 0 when the system has no solution, 1 when it has a unique solution, and 2 when it has infinitely many solutions. For a unique solution, the values of x and y shall be written to the REAL output variables SolutionX and SolutionY. When the system has no solution or infinitely many solutions, SolutionX and SolutionY shall both be set to 0.0.

title: Cubic Bezier Curve Point Calculation
requirement: Design an LD program that reads eight REAL input variables, P0X, P0Y, P1X, P1Y, P2X, P2Y, P3X, and P3Y, representing four two-dimensional control points P0, P1, P2, and P3 of a cubic Bezier curve. The program shall also read the REAL input variable ParameterT, which shall be within the range from 0.0 to 1.0. The program shall calculate the coordinates of the corresponding point on the cubic Bezier curve and write them to the REAL output variables CurveX and CurveY.

title: Area of a Convex Pentagon
requirement: Design an LD program that reads ten REAL input variables, X1, Y1, X2, Y2, X3, Y3, X4, Y4, X5, and Y5, representing the five vertices of a convex pentagon. The vertices shall be given consecutively along the pentagon boundary in either clockwise or counterclockwise order. The program shall calculate the area of the pentagon and write the non-negative result to the REAL output variable Area.
input_constraints: The five points form a convex pentagon.
The vertices are given consecutively in clockwise or counterclockwise order.

title: Triangle Classification by Side Lengths
requirement: Design an LD function that reads three positive DINT input variables, SideA, SideB, and SideC, representing the three side lengths of a potential triangle. The program shall determine whether the side lengths form a valid triangle and classify a valid triangle according to its side lengths. The BOOL output IsValid shall be TRUE if the side lengths form a valid triangle. For a valid triangle, exactly one of the BOOL outputs IsEquilateral, IsIsosceles, and IsScalene shall be TRUE. IsEquilateral shall indicate that all three sides are equal. IsIsosceles shall indicate that exactly two sides are equal. IsScalene shall indicate that all three sides are different. If the side lengths do not form a valid triangle, all four outputs shall be FALSE. The result shall be independent of the input order.

title: Plane Equation from Three Points
requirement: Design an LD function that reads nine REAL input variables representing three non-collinear points P1, P2, and P3 in three-dimensional Cartesian space. The coordinates of P1 are P1X, P1Y, and P1Z; the coordinates of P2 are P2X, P2Y, and P2Z; and the coordinates of P3 are P3X, P3Y, and P3Z. The program shall calculate the coefficients A, B, C, and D of the plane equation A * x + B * y + C * z + D = 0. The normal vector (A, B, C) shall be calculated using the ordered cross product (P2 - P1) cross (P3 - P1). The coefficients shall not be normalized.
input_constraints: P1, P2, and P3 are distinct and non-collinear.

title: Bilinear Interpolation
requirement: Design an LD program that reads four REAL input variables, Q11, Q21, Q12, and Q22, representing values at the four corners of a rectangular grid cell. The program shall also read two normalized REAL position parameters, U and V, each within the range from 0.0 to 1.0. U represents the relative horizontal position from the Q11-Q12 side toward the Q21-Q22 side, and V represents the relative vertical position from the Q11-Q21 side toward the Q12-Q22 side. The program shall calculate the bilinearly interpolated value and write it to the REAL output variable Result.

title: Two-Dimensional Rotation Transformation
requirement: Design an LD program that reads the REAL coordinates X and Y of a two-dimensional point and a REAL rotation angle Angle. Angle shall be expressed in radians. The program shall rotate the point counterclockwise around the origin by Angle and write the transformed coordinates to the REAL output variables RotatedX and RotatedY. A negative value of Angle shall produce a clockwise rotation.

title: Intersection of Two Lines
requirement: Design an LD program that reads eight REAL input variables representing two non-parallel straight lines in a two-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system. The first line passes through the points P1 and P2, whose coordinates are P1X, P1Y, P2X, and P2Y. The second line passes through the points P3 and P4, whose coordinates are P3X, P3Y, P4X, and P4Y. The program shall calculate the intersection point of the two infinite straight lines and write its coordinates to the REAL output variables IntersectionX and IntersectionY.
input_constraints: P1 and P2 are distinct.
P3 and P4 are distinct.
The two straight lines are not parallel.

title: Great-Circle Distance Between Two Points
requirement: Design an LD function that reads the three-dimensional Cartesian coordinates of two points located on the surface of a sphere centered at the origin. The coordinates of the first point are X1, Y1, and Z1, and the coordinates of the second point are X2, Y2, and Z2. The REAL input variable Radius represents the sphere radius and shall be greater than 0.0. The program shall calculate the length of the shorter great-circle arc between the two points and write the result to the REAL output variable GreatCircleDistance. The benchmark inputs guarantee that both points lie on the specified sphere.
input_constraints: X1 * X1 + Y1 * Y1 + Z1 * Z1 = Radius * Radius within the benchmark tolerance.
X2 * X2 + Y2 * Y2 + Z2 * Z2 = Radius * Radius within the benchmark tolerance.

title: Intersection Points of an Ellipse and a Line
requirement: Design an LD function that calculates the two distinct intersection points between an axis-aligned ellipse centered at the origin and an infinite straight line. The ellipse is defined by x^2 / SemiAxisA^2 + y^2 / SemiAxisB^2 = 1, where the REAL inputs SemiAxisA and SemiAxisB are greater than 0.0. The line is defined parametrically by x = LineX + t * DirectionX and y = LineY + t * DirectionY. DirectionX and DirectionY shall not both be 0.0. The benchmark inputs guarantee that the line intersects the ellipse at two distinct points. The intersection corresponding to the positive square-root term shall be written to Intersection1X and Intersection1Y, and the intersection corresponding to the negative square-root term shall be written to Intersection2X and Intersection2Y.
input_constraints: DirectionX * DirectionX + DirectionY * DirectionY > 0.0.
The resulting quadratic discriminant is greater than 0.0.

title: Four-Point Concyclicity Test
requirement: Design an LD function that reads eight DINT input variables, X1, Y1, X2, Y2, X3, Y3, X4, and Y4, representing four distinct points in a two-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system. The first three points shall not be collinear. The program shall determine whether all four points lie on the same circle and write the result to the BOOL output variable IsConcyclic. Each coordinate shall be within the range from -50 to 50.
input_constraints: The four points are distinct.
The first three points are not collinear.

title: Least-Squares Line Fitting for Three Points
requirement: Design an LD program that reads six REAL input variables, X1, Y1, X2, Y2, X3, and Y3, representing three data points in a two-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system. The program shall use the ordinary least-squares method to fit a straight line of the form y = Slope * x + Intercept. The fitted slope shall be written to the REAL output variable Slope, and the fitted intercept shall be written to the REAL output variable Intercept. The benchmark inputs guarantee that the three x-coordinates are not all equal, so the fitted slope and intercept are uniquely defined. The result shall be independent of the order in which the three points are provided.
input_constraints: X1, X2, and X3 are not all equal.

title: Scaled Taylor Approximation of the Exponential Function
requirement: Design an LD program that approximates the exponential function e^X using scaling, a five-term Maclaurin expansion, and repeated squaring. The REAL input variable X shall be within the range from -4.0 to 4.0. The program shall first calculate ScaledX = X / 8.0. It shall then calculate the first five terms of the Maclaurin expansion of e^ScaledX, including the constant term, and write the result to ScaledTaylor. The program shall approximate e^X by raising ScaledTaylor to the eighth power through three consecutive squaring operations and write the result to ApproxExp.

title: Singular Value Decomposition of a Restricted 2x2 Matrix
requirement: Design an LD program that calculates the singular value decomposition of a real 2x2 symmetric positive-definite matrix A. The matrix is defined as A = [[A11, A12], [A12, A22]]. The benchmark inputs guarantee that A11 > A22 > 0.0, A12 > 0.0, and A11 * A22 - A12 * A12 > 0.0. These constraints guarantee two distinct positive singular values. The program shall calculate the singular values Sigma1 and Sigma2 in descending order. It shall use the fixed convention U = V = R, where R is the rotation matrix defined by Theta = 0.5 * ATAN(2.0 * A12 / (A11 - A22)). The program shall output all elements of U and V. The decomposition shall satisfy A = U * Sigma * transpose(V), where Sigma is the diagonal matrix with Sigma1 and Sigma2.

title: Numerical Integration of a Polynomial Using Composite Simpson's Rule
requirement: Design an LD program that numerically integrates a fourth-degree polynomial over a specified interval using the composite Simpson's one-third rule with eight equal subintervals. The polynomial is defined as f(x) = C4 * x^4 + C3 * x^3 + C2 * x^2 + C1 * x + C0. The REAL inputs LowerBound and UpperBound define the integration interval and shall satisfy LowerBound < UpperBound. The program shall evaluate the polynomial at nine equally spaced points, calculate the Simpson approximation, and write it to the REAL output ApproxIntegral. The program shall also calculate the exact integral from the polynomial antiderivative and output ExactIntegral and AbsoluteError. The nine function values shall be obtained from the supplied coefficients rather than from a textual mathematical expression.
input_constraints: LowerBound < UpperBound.

title: Four-Point Discrete Fourier Transform
requirement: Design an LD function that calculates the unnormalized four-point forward discrete Fourier transform of four REAL time-domain samples X0, X1, X2, and X3. The transform shall use the convention F[k] = sum from n = 0 to 3 of Xn * exp(-j * 2 * pi * k * n / 4). The program shall output the real and imaginary parts of all four frequency bins. It shall also calculate the magnitude and power of each frequency bin. The outputs shall not be divided by the number of samples.

title: Ascending Sort of Six DINT Values
requirement: Design an LD program that reads six DINT input variables, Value1, Value2, Value3, Value4, Value5, and Value6, and sorts them in ascending numerical order. The six sorted values shall be written to the DINT output variables Sorted1, Sorted2, Sorted3, Sorted4, Sorted5, and Sorted6, where Sorted1 is the smallest value and Sorted6 is the largest value. Duplicate values and negative values shall be preserved. The output sequence shall contain exactly the same multiset of values as the input sequence. Any correct sorting method may be used. Because the task uses a fixed number of inputs, the sorting operations may be implemented as an explicitly unrolled sequence of compare-and-exchange operations without arrays, loops, or dynamic indexing.

title: Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix
requirement: Design an LD program that calculates the inverse of a real 3x3 matrix. The matrix is defined by nine REAL input variables A11, A12, A13, A21, A22, A23, A31, A32, and A33. The benchmark inputs guarantee that the matrix is invertible and that the absolute value of its determinant is at least 0.1. The program shall calculate the determinant and the nine elements of the inverse matrix. The inverse matrix shall satisfy A * InverseA = I within the specified numerical tolerance.
input_constraints: The matrix is invertible.
ABS(Determinant) >= 0.1.

title: Delayed Motor Start
requirement: Design an LD function that delays the start of a motor using an on-delay timer. When the BOOL input StartCommand remains TRUE continuously, the timer shall begin timing. After the user-specified TIME input DelayTime has elapsed, the BOOL output MotorOutput shall become TRUE. If StartCommand becomes FALSE before DelayTime has elapsed, the timer shall reset and MotorOutput shall remain FALSE. If StartCommand becomes FALSE after the motor has started, MotorOutput shall immediately become FALSE and the timer shall reset.

title: Sensor Pulse Counter with Alarm
requirement: Design an LD function block that counts objects detected by a sensor. Each rising edge of the BOOL input SensorPulse shall increase the DINT output CurrentCount by one. Keeping SensorPulse continuously TRUE for multiple PLC scans shall count as only one object. The DINT input TargetCount specifies the alarm threshold. When CurrentCount is greater than or equal to TargetCount, the BOOL output CountAlarm shall become TRUE. When the BOOL input Reset is TRUE, CurrentCount shall be reset to zero and CountAlarm shall become FALSE. Reset shall have priority over counting.

title: Two-Button AND Motor Control
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a motor using two BOOL push-button inputs, ButtonA and ButtonB. The BOOL output MotorOutput shall be TRUE only when ButtonA and ButtonB are both TRUE. If either button is FALSE, MotorOutput shall be FALSE. The control shall be combinational and shall not include latching or retained state.

title: Two-Button OR Motor Control
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a motor using two BOOL push-button inputs, ButtonA and ButtonB. The BOOL output MotorOutput shall be TRUE when at least one of the two buttons is TRUE. MotorOutput shall be FALSE only when both buttons are FALSE. The control shall be combinational and shall not include latching or retained state.

title: Four-Channel Temperature Alarm
requirement: Design an LD program that monitors four REAL temperature inputs, Temperature1, Temperature2, Temperature3, and Temperature4. The REAL input HighTemperatureLimit specifies a common upper temperature limit for all four channels. The BOOL output HighTemperatureAlarm shall become TRUE when at least one temperature is greater than HighTemperatureLimit. If all four temperatures are less than or equal to HighTemperatureLimit, HighTemperatureAlarm shall be FALSE. The alarm logic shall be combinational and shall not include latching, delay, or retained state.

title: Automatic Water Heater Control
requirement: Design an LD function block that automatically controls a water heater according to the measured water temperature. The REAL input WaterTemperature represents the current water temperature, and the REAL input TemperatureSetpoint represents the desired upper temperature limit. The BOOL output HeaterOutput shall be TRUE when WaterTemperature is lower than TemperatureSetpoint. HeaterOutput shall be FALSE when WaterTemperature is greater than or equal to TemperatureSetpoint. The control shall be combinational and shall not include hysteresis, delay, latching, or retained state.

title: Latched Safety Light Curtain Interlock
requirement: Design an LD function block that interlocks a press machine with a safety light curtain. The BOOL input PressRunCommand represents the command to operate the press. The BOOL input LightCurtainBlocked is TRUE when the safety light curtain is obstructed, and the BOOL input ManualReset represents an operator reset command. When LightCurtainBlocked becomes TRUE, the program shall immediately stop the press, set the BOOL output PanelLocked to TRUE, and latch the safety interlock. After the light curtain becomes clear, the safety interlock shall remain latched and PanelLocked shall remain TRUE. The interlock shall be cleared only when LightCurtainBlocked is FALSE and ManualReset is TRUE; a valid reset shall set PanelLocked to FALSE. A reset command applied while the light curtain is blocked shall have no effect. The light-curtain fault condition shall have priority over the reset command. After the interlock has been cleared, PressOutput shall follow PressRunCommand.

title: Dual Safety Door Interlock
requirement: Design an LD program that interlocks a machine with two safety doors. The BOOL inputs SafetyDoor1Closed and SafetyDoor2Closed are TRUE when the corresponding safety doors are fully closed. The BOOL input StartCommand represents the command to operate the machine. The BOOL output MachineOutput shall be TRUE only when StartCommand, SafetyDoor1Closed, and SafetyDoor2Closed are all TRUE. If either safety door is open, MachineOutput shall immediately become FALSE, including when the machine is already operating. The control shall be combinational and shall not include latching, delay, or manual reset.

title: Three-Button Emergency Stop System
requirement: Design an LD program that provides emergency-stop protection for a production line containing a conveyor, a feeder, and a packaging machine. The BOOL inputs EmergencyStop1Pressed, EmergencyStop2Pressed, and EmergencyStop3Pressed are TRUE when the corresponding emergency-stop buttons are pressed. The BOOL inputs ConveyorRunCommand, FeederRunCommand, and PackagingRunCommand represent the operating commands for the three devices. If any emergency-stop input is TRUE, the BOOL outputs ConveyorOutput, FeederOutput, and PackagingOutput shall all immediately become FALSE. When no emergency-stop button is pressed, each device output shall follow its corresponding run command. The control shall be combinational and shall not include fault latching or manual reset.

title: Delayed Equipment Stop
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a device using a fixed one-second off-delay. When the BOOL input RunCommand becomes TRUE, the BOOL output EquipmentOutput shall become TRUE immediately. When RunCommand becomes FALSE after the device has been running, EquipmentOutput shall remain TRUE for one second and then become FALSE. If RunCommand becomes TRUE again before the one-second off-delay has elapsed, the pending stop shall be cancelled and EquipmentOutput shall remain TRUE. If RunCommand is FALSE before the device has been started, EquipmentOutput shall remain FALSE.

title: Packaging Completion One-Shot Pulse
requirement: Design an LD program that generates a one-scan transfer pulse when a packaging operation is completed. The BOOL input PackagingComplete represents the completion signal from the packaging equipment. Each time PackagingComplete changes from FALSE to TRUE, the BOOL output TransferPulse shall become TRUE for exactly one PLC scan. If PackagingComplete remains TRUE for multiple scans, TransferPulse shall return to FALSE after the first scan and shall not be generated again. A new TransferPulse shall be generated only after PackagingComplete has first returned to FALSE and then changes to TRUE again.

title: Two-Out-of-Three Sensor Voting
requirement: Design an LD program that performs two-out-of-three voting on three BOOL sensor inputs, Sensor1, Sensor2, and Sensor3. The BOOL output VoteValid shall be TRUE when at least two of the three sensor inputs are TRUE. VoteValid shall be FALSE when fewer than two sensor inputs are TRUE. The logic shall be combinational and shall not include latching, delay, or retained state.

title: Motor Start-Stop Self-Holding Control
requirement: Design an LD function block that controls a motor using a start button and a stop button. When the BOOL input StartButton is pressed, the BOOL output MotorOutput shall become TRUE and remain TRUE after StartButton is released. When the BOOL input StopButton is pressed, MotorOutput shall immediately become FALSE and remain FALSE after StopButton is released. The motor shall remain stopped until StartButton is pressed again. StopButton shall have priority over StartButton when both inputs are TRUE in the same PLC scan.

title: 4–20 mA Analog Signal Scaling
requirement: Design an LD function that converts a REAL 4–20 mA analog input signal into a REAL measurement value ranging from 0.0% to 100.0%. When CurrentInput is less than or equal to 4.0 mA, ScaledValue shall be 0.0. When CurrentInput is greater than or equal to 20.0 mA, ScaledValue shall be 100.0. When CurrentInput is between 4.0 mA and 20.0 mA, ScaledValue shall be calculated using linear scaling.

title: Fixed-Duration Buzzer Pulse
requirement: Design an LD program that activates a buzzer for a fixed duration when a trigger signal is received. Each time the BOOL input TriggerButton changes from FALSE to TRUE, the BOOL output BuzzerOutput shall immediately become TRUE and remain TRUE for three seconds. After three seconds, BuzzerOutput shall automatically become FALSE even if TriggerButton remains TRUE. Keeping TriggerButton continuously TRUE shall not extend or retrigger the pulse. A new three-second pulse may be generated only after TriggerButton has returned to FALSE and then changes to TRUE again.

title: Limit Switch Controlled Equipment Stop
requirement: Design an LD program that controls the start and stop of a moving device using a limit switch. Pressing the BOOL input StartButton shall start the device if the BOOL input LimitSwitchReached is FALSE. After the device starts, it shall remain running when StartButton is released. When LimitSwitchReached becomes TRUE, the BOOL output DeviceOutput shall immediately become FALSE and remain FALSE. The device shall also stop when the BOOL input StopButton is TRUE. The device shall not restart while LimitSwitchReached remains TRUE. After the limit switch is cleared, the operator must press StartButton again to restart the device. StopButton and LimitSwitchReached shall have priority over StartButton.

title: Sequential Start of Three Devices
requirement: Design an LD function block that starts three devices in the fixed sequence Device A, Device B, and Device C. When the BOOL input StartButton is pressed, the sequence shall become active and the BOOL output DeviceAOutput shall become TRUE immediately. After the BOOL input DeviceAFeedback has remained TRUE continuously for one second, the BOOL output DeviceBOutput shall become TRUE. After DeviceBOutput has started and the BOOL input DeviceBFeedback has remained TRUE continuously for one second, the BOOL output DeviceCOutput shall become TRUE. A downstream device shall not start unless the preceding device has provided its running feedback. If DeviceAFeedback becomes FALSE, the timer for Device B shall reset and DeviceBOutput and DeviceCOutput shall become FALSE. If DeviceBFeedback becomes FALSE, the timer for Device C shall reset and DeviceCOutput shall become FALSE. When the BOOL input StopButton is TRUE, all three outputs shall immediately become FALSE, both timers and the sequence state shall reset, and a new sequence shall require StartButton to be pressed again.

title: Forward-Reverse Motor Control with Latched Overload Protection
requirement: Design an LD function block that controls a motor in forward and reverse directions with mutual interlocking and latched overload protection. When ForwardStartButton is TRUE while the motor is stopped, ForwardOutput shall become TRUE and remain TRUE after the button is released. ReverseStartButton shall operate ReverseOutput in the same way. While one direction is running, the start command for the opposite direction shall be ignored. If both start buttons are TRUE while the motor is stopped, neither direction shall start. StopButton shall immediately set both direction outputs to FALSE. If OverloadActive becomes TRUE, both direction outputs shall immediately become FALSE and OverloadAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. When ManualReset is TRUE and OverloadActive is FALSE, OverloadAlarm shall be cleared. If ManualReset is TRUE while OverloadActive is TRUE, the reset command shall have no effect. While OverloadAlarm is TRUE, neither direction may start. StopButton and OverloadActive shall have priority over the start commands.

title: Automatic Door Sequence Control
requirement: Design an LD function block that controls an automatic door using an infrared presence sensor, an obstacle sensor, and door limit switches. When InfraredDetected is TRUE and DoorOpenLimit is FALSE, OpenDoorOutput shall be TRUE. After InfraredDetected and ObstacleDetected have both remained FALSE continuously for one second, CloseDoorOutput shall become TRUE and remain TRUE until DoorClosedLimit becomes TRUE. If InfraredDetected or ObstacleDetected becomes TRUE during the one-second delay or while the door is closing, CloseDoorOutput shall immediately become FALSE and the one-second delay shall reset. OpenDoorOutput and CloseDoorOutput shall never be TRUE at the same time.
input_constraints: DoorOpenLimit and DoorClosedLimit shall not both be TRUE at the same time.

title: Forward-Reverse Motor Control with Reversal Delay
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a motor in forward and reverse directions with a three-second reversal delay. When the motor is stopped, ForwardStartButton shall start ForwardOutput immediately and ReverseStartButton shall start ReverseOutput immediately. The selected direction shall remain active after its start button is released. If the opposite start button becomes TRUE while the motor is running, the active output shall immediately become FALSE and a three-second delay shall begin. The opposite start button must remain TRUE continuously during the full delay; otherwise the reversal shall be cancelled and the motor shall remain stopped. After the delay, the requested opposite direction shall start and remain active. StopButton shall immediately set both outputs to FALSE and cancel any reversal delay. If both direction start buttons are TRUE while the motor is stopped, neither direction shall start. ForwardOutput and ReverseOutput shall never be TRUE at the same time.

title: Bounded Bidirectional Counter
requirement: Design an LD program that implements a bidirectional counter with a permitted range from 0 to 5. Each time the BOOL input IncrementButton changes from FALSE to TRUE, the DINT output CurrentCount shall increase by one. Each time the BOOL input DecrementButton changes from FALSE to TRUE, CurrentCount shall decrease by one. Keeping either button continuously TRUE shall not cause repeated counting. CurrentCount shall not increase above 5 and shall not decrease below 0. When the BOOL input ResetButton is TRUE, CurrentCount shall immediately become zero. ResetButton shall have priority over increment and decrement operations. If IncrementButton and DecrementButton both produce a rising edge during the same PLC scan, CurrentCount shall remain unchanged. The BOOL output LowerLimitReached shall be TRUE when CurrentCount equals 0. The BOOL output UpperLimitReached shall be TRUE when CurrentCount equals 5.

title: Two-Level Temperature Alarm
requirement: Design an LD program that implements a two-level temperature alarm. When the REAL input EquipmentTemperature is lower than 80.0 degrees Celsius, both the BOOL output YellowWarning and the BOOL output RedAlarm shall be FALSE. When EquipmentTemperature is greater than or equal to 80.0 degrees Celsius but lower than 100.0 degrees Celsius, YellowWarning shall be TRUE and RedAlarm shall be FALSE. When EquipmentTemperature is greater than or equal to 100.0 degrees Celsius, RedAlarm shall be TRUE and YellowWarning shall be FALSE. RedAlarm shall have priority over YellowWarning, and the two alarm outputs shall never be TRUE at the same time.

title: Three-Sensor Material Weight Classification
requirement: Design an LD function block that classifies material weight using three REAL pressure sensor measurements. The REAL output TotalWeight shall equal the sum of PressureSensor1, PressureSensor2, and PressureSensor3. When the BOOL input MaterialPresent is FALSE, the BOOL outputs LightWeight, MediumWeight, and HeavyWeight shall all be FALSE. When MaterialPresent is TRUE and TotalWeight is lower than 30.0 kilograms, LightWeight shall be TRUE. When MaterialPresent is TRUE and TotalWeight is greater than or equal to 30.0 kilograms but lower than 75.0 kilograms, MediumWeight shall be TRUE. When MaterialPresent is TRUE and TotalWeight is greater than or equal to 75.0 kilograms, HeavyWeight shall be TRUE. The three weight classification outputs shall be mutually exclusive.
input_constraints: PressureSensor1, PressureSensor2, and PressureSensor3 are nonnegative.

title: Occupancy and Daylight Based Lighting Control
requirement: Design an LD program that selects one of three lighting levels according to the DINT input OccupancyCount and the REAL input DaylightLevel. When OccupancyCount is between 1 and 5 inclusive and DaylightLevel is greater than or equal to 70.0 percent, the BOOL output LowLightingOutput shall be TRUE. When OccupancyCount is between 1 and 5 inclusive and DaylightLevel is greater than or equal to 30.0 percent but lower than 70.0 percent, MediumLightingOutput shall be TRUE. When OccupancyCount is between 1 and 5 inclusive and DaylightLevel is lower than 30.0 percent, HighLightingOutput shall be TRUE. When OccupancyCount is greater than 5 and DaylightLevel is greater than or equal to 70.0 percent, MediumLightingOutput shall be TRUE. When OccupancyCount is greater than 5 and DaylightLevel is lower than 70.0 percent, HighLightingOutput shall be TRUE. When OccupancyCount changes to 0, the currently active lighting level shall remain active for three seconds. If OccupancyCount remains 0 for the full three seconds, all lighting outputs shall become FALSE. If OccupancyCount becomes greater than 0 before the delay expires, the timer shall reset and the lighting level shall immediately be recalculated from the current occupancy and daylight values. LowLightingOutput, MediumLightingOutput, and HighLightingOutput shall be mutually exclusive.
input_constraints: OccupancyCount >= 0.
0.0 <= DaylightLevel <= 100.0.

title: Weekday and Weekend Scheduled Lighting Control
requirement: Design an LD function block that controls a lighting output according to the current day and time. The DINT input DayOfWeek uses values 1 through 7, where 1 represents Monday and 7 represents Sunday. Monday through Friday are weekdays, and Saturday and Sunday are weekends. On weekdays, the BOOL output LightingOutput shall be TRUE from 18:00 inclusive until 06:00 exclusive. On weekends, LightingOutput shall be TRUE from 19:00 inclusive until 05:00 exclusive. The schedule shall be selected from the current value of DayOfWeek at each PLC scan. LightingOutput shall be FALSE outside the applicable lighting period.
input_constraints: 1 <= DayOfWeek <= 7.
0 <= CurrentHour <= 23.
0 <= CurrentMinute <= 59.

title: Single-Bottle Flow-Pulse Filling Control
requirement: Design an LD program that fills one bottle at a time using a bottle-position sensor and flow-meter pulses. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of StartButton shall start a filling cycle only when BottleAtFillPosition is TRUE and the controller is idle. At cycle start, CurrentFillVolume shall reset to 0 and FillValveOutput shall become TRUE. Each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of FlowPulse while the valve is open represents 20 milliliters and shall increase CurrentFillVolume by 20. Keeping FlowPulse continuously TRUE shall not cause repeated counting. When CurrentFillVolume reaches 100 milliliters, it shall be clamped at 100, FillValveOutput shall become FALSE, and ConveyorOutput shall become TRUE. ConveyorOutput shall remain TRUE until BottleAtFillPosition becomes FALSE, after which the conveyor shall stop and the controller shall return to idle. The next bottle shall not start automatically; a new StartButton transition is required. StopButton shall immediately stop both outputs, cancel the current cycle, and reset CurrentFillVolume to 0.

title: Temperature-Controlled Fan with Manual Override
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a ventilation fan using temperature hysteresis and a manual override. In automatic operation, when the REAL input Temperature becomes greater than 30.0 degrees Celsius, the retained automatic fan state shall become TRUE. Once started automatically, the fan shall remain active until Temperature becomes lower than 25.0 degrees Celsius. When Temperature is between 25.0 and 30.0 degrees Celsius inclusive, the automatic fan state shall retain its previous value. When the BOOL input ManualForceVentilation is TRUE, the BOOL output FanOutput shall be TRUE regardless of Temperature. When ManualForceVentilation returns to FALSE, FanOutput shall again follow the retained automatic fan state. The automatic fan state shall continue to respond to Temperature while manual override is active. The initial automatic fan state shall be FALSE.

title: Cyclic Conveyor Timing Control
requirement: Design an LD function block that operates a conveyor in a repeating timed cycle. Pressing the BOOL input StartButton shall activate the automatic cycle and retain the active state after the button is released. After the cycle starts, the system shall first wait for three seconds with the BOOL output ConveyorOutput set to FALSE. When the three-second waiting period is complete, ConveyorOutput shall become TRUE and remain TRUE for one second. After the one-second running period is complete, ConveyorOutput shall become FALSE and a new three-second waiting period shall begin. The three-second waiting and one-second running phases shall repeat continuously while the system remains active. When the BOOL input StopButton is TRUE, ConveyorOutput shall immediately become FALSE, the automatic cycle shall reset, and all timer states shall be cleared. A subsequent start shall begin with a new three-second waiting period. StopButton shall have priority over StartButton.

title: Sequential Start and Stop of Three Conveyors
requirement: Design an LD program that controls three conveyors with sequential starting, reverse-order stopping, running feedback, and emergency-stop protection. Pressing StartButton shall begin the start sequence and set Conveyor1Output to TRUE immediately. After Conveyor1Feedback has remained TRUE continuously for one second, Conveyor2Output shall become TRUE. After Conveyor2Feedback has then remained TRUE continuously for one second, Conveyor3Output shall become TRUE. If a feedback signal becomes FALSE before its corresponding start delay is complete, that timer shall reset. Once started, each conveyor output shall remain TRUE until a stop sequence or EmergencyStop occurs. Pressing StopButton shall begin the stop sequence: Conveyor3Output shall become FALSE immediately, Conveyor2Output shall become FALSE when Conveyor3Feedback is FALSE, and Conveyor1Output shall become FALSE when Conveyor2Feedback is FALSE. No additional stop-delay timers are required. EmergencyStop shall immediately set all three outputs to FALSE and reset the sequence and timers.

title: Empty Bottle Detection and Delayed Rejection
requirement: Design an LD program that detects and rejects empty bottles on a production line. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of the BOOL input BottleDetected indicates that a new bottle has entered the inspection position. At that transition, the BOOL input ContentDetected shall be sampled once. If ContentDetected is FALSE, the bottle shall be classified as empty and a pending rejection task shall be retained. If ContentDetected is TRUE, no rejection task shall be created. For an empty bottle, the system shall wait for two seconds after the detection transition and then set the BOOL output RejectOutput to TRUE for exactly five hundred milliseconds. RejectOutput shall then automatically return to FALSE. Keeping BottleDetected continuously TRUE shall not create repeated inspection or rejection events. The next bottle may be evaluated only after BottleDetected has returned to FALSE and then changes to TRUE again. The production line guarantees that successive bottle-detection rising edges are separated by more than 2.5 seconds, so only one rejection task needs to be processed at a time. When the BOOL input ResetButton is TRUE, any pending rejection task, transport-delay timer, and rejection pulse shall be cancelled, and RejectOutput shall immediately become FALSE. ResetButton shall have priority over bottle detection.
input_constraints: Successive FALSE-to-TRUE transitions of BottleDetected are separated by more than 2500 milliseconds.

title: Weekly Scheduled Alarm Test with Manual Trigger
requirement: Design an LD program that automatically tests an alarm every Monday at 10:00:00. The DINT input DayOfWeek uses values 1 through 7, where 1 represents Monday. When the current time first becomes Monday at 10:00:00, the BOOL output AlarmOutput shall become TRUE and remain TRUE for three seconds. The scheduled condition shall trigger only once when it changes from FALSE to TRUE and shall not repeatedly trigger during consecutive PLC scans within the same second. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of the BOOL input ManualTestButton shall also start a three-second alarm test. Keeping ManualTestButton continuously TRUE shall not repeatedly trigger the alarm. While AlarmOutput is already TRUE, additional scheduled or manual triggers shall be ignored and shall not extend or restart the current three-second test period. After the test period ends, AlarmOutput shall automatically become FALSE.
input_constraints: 1 <= DayOfWeek <= 7.
0 <= CurrentHour <= 23.
0 <= CurrentMinute <= 59.
0 <= CurrentSecond <= 59.

title: Delayed Automatic Faucet Control
requirement: Design an LD program that controls an automatic faucet using a presence sensor. The BOOL input PresenceDetected must remain continuously TRUE for one second before the BOOL output WaterValveOutput becomes TRUE. If PresenceDetected becomes FALSE before the one-second delay is complete, the delay shall reset and the faucet shall remain closed. Once WaterValveOutput becomes TRUE, it shall remain TRUE for three seconds even if PresenceDetected becomes FALSE. Changes in PresenceDetected during the three-second water cycle shall not restart or extend the cycle. After three seconds, WaterValveOutput shall automatically become FALSE. If PresenceDetected remains TRUE when the water cycle ends, a new cycle shall not begin. PresenceDetected must first become FALSE to rearm the system and then remain continuously TRUE for another one second before a new water cycle can start.

title: Redundant Main and Backup Pump Control
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a main pump and a backup pump for redundant operation. When the BOOL input RunDemand is TRUE and the BOOL input MainPumpFault is FALSE, the BOOL output MainPumpOutput shall be TRUE and the BOOL output BackupPumpOutput shall be FALSE. If MainPumpFault becomes TRUE while RunDemand is TRUE, MainPumpOutput shall immediately become FALSE, a retained backup-selection state shall be set, and BackupPumpOutput shall become TRUE if the BOOL input BackupPumpFault is FALSE. If MainPumpFault is already TRUE when RunDemand becomes TRUE, the backup pump shall be selected immediately. Once the backup pump has been selected during a run cycle, the system shall continue to use the backup pump even if MainPumpFault later becomes FALSE. The backup-selection state shall reset only when RunDemand becomes FALSE. If BackupPumpFault is TRUE while the backup pump is selected, both pump outputs shall be FALSE and the BOOL output PumpSystemAlarm shall be TRUE. If BackupPumpFault subsequently becomes FALSE while RunDemand remains TRUE, BackupPumpOutput shall resume and PumpSystemAlarm shall become FALSE. A backup-pump fault alone shall not prevent the main pump from operating while the main pump is healthy. When RunDemand is FALSE, both pump outputs and PumpSystemAlarm shall be FALSE and the backup-selection state shall reset. MainPumpOutput and BackupPumpOutput shall never be TRUE at the same time.

title: Batch Counting with Timed Conveyor Pause
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a conveyor and counts products in repeated batches. Pressing the BOOL input StartButton shall activate the system and retain the active state after the button is released. While the system is active and not in a batch pause, the BOOL output ConveyorOutput shall be TRUE. Each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of the BOOL input ProductDetected while ConveyorOutput is TRUE shall increase the DINT output CurrentBatchCount by one. Keeping ProductDetected continuously TRUE shall not cause repeated counting. Product-detection transitions received while the system is inactive or while the conveyor is paused shall be ignored. When CurrentBatchCount first reaches 5, ConveyorOutput shall immediately become FALSE, the BOOL output BatchCompletePulse shall become TRUE for one PLC scan, and a one-second batch pause shall begin. When the one-second pause is complete, CurrentBatchCount shall reset to 0 and ConveyorOutput shall automatically become TRUE to begin the next batch. When the BOOL input StopButton is TRUE, ConveyorOutput shall immediately become FALSE, the active state, batch count, pause timer, and completion pulse shall reset. Clearing StopButton shall not restart the system; a new StartButton command shall be required. StopButton shall have priority over StartButton.

title: Compressor Pressure Control with Restart Delay
requirement: Design an LD program that controls an air compressor using pressure hysteresis and a minimum restart delay. When the BOOL input SystemEnable is TRUE and the REAL input TankPressure is lower than 4.0 bar, the BOOL output CompressorOutput shall become TRUE, provided that no restart delay is active. Once started, the compressor shall remain active until TankPressure becomes greater than or equal to 7.0 bar. When TankPressure reaches or exceeds 7.0 bar, CompressorOutput shall become FALSE and a one-second restart delay shall begin. During the restart delay, CompressorOutput shall remain FALSE even if TankPressure falls below 4.0 bar. When the one-second delay is complete, the BOOL output RestartDelayActive shall become FALSE. If SystemEnable is still TRUE and TankPressure is below 4.0 bar at that time, the compressor shall restart immediately. If TankPressure is greater than or equal to 4.0 bar, the compressor shall remain stopped. When SystemEnable becomes FALSE, CompressorOutput shall immediately become FALSE, the retained compressor state and restart-delay timer shall reset, and RestartDelayActive shall become FALSE. A subsequent enable command may start the compressor immediately if TankPressure is below 4.0 bar.
input_constraints: TankPressure >= 0.0.

title: Timed Five-Person Voting System
requirement: Design an LD program that manages a three-second voting session for five voters. Each voter is represented by a DINT input with three valid states: 0 = NotVoted, 1 = Agree, and 2 = Disagree. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of the BOOL input StartVoteButton shall start a voting session if no voting session is active and no previous result is waiting for reset. The BOOL output VotingActive shall become TRUE when a session starts, remain TRUE throughout the three-second voting period, and become FALSE when the period expires or ResetButton is activated. During the three-second voting period, voters may change their selections and the DINT outputs AgreeCount, DisagreeCount, and NotVotedCount shall continuously reflect the current five vote inputs. When the three-second voting period expires, the current vote states shall be used to determine and latch the final counts and voting result. If fewer than three voters have cast either an Agree or Disagree vote, the BOOL output InsufficientVotes shall be TRUE. If at least three voters have voted and AgreeCount is greater than DisagreeCount, Approved shall be TRUE. If at least three voters have voted and DisagreeCount is greater than AgreeCount, Rejected shall be TRUE. If at least three voters have voted and AgreeCount equals DisagreeCount, TieResult shall be TRUE. Approved, Rejected, TieResult, and InsufficientVotes shall be mutually exclusive. After the voting period ends, the final counts and result shall remain unchanged even if the vote inputs change. A new StartVoteButton command shall be ignored until the BOOL input ResetButton becomes TRUE. ResetButton shall clear the voting state, timer, counts, and result outputs and shall have priority over StartVoteButton.
input_constraints: Each vote input shall be 0, 1, or 2.
0 = NotVoted, 1 = Agree, 2 = Disagree.

title: Conveyor Slow-Transit and Jam Detection
requirement: Design an LD program that monitors the travel time of one item between an entry sensor and an exit sensor. When SystemEnable is TRUE and JamAlarm is FALSE, ConveyorOutput shall be TRUE. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of EntrySensor shall start tracking an item when no item is already being tracked and shall set the BOOL output ItemTrackingActive to TRUE. If ExitSensor becomes TRUE while an item is being tracked and fewer than two seconds have elapsed, tracking shall end normally, ItemTrackingActive shall become FALSE, and the timer shall reset. If the item has not reached the exit after one second, SlowTransitWarning shall become TRUE. If the item has not reached the exit after two seconds, JamAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched, ItemTrackingActive and the warning shall become FALSE, and ConveyorOutput shall become FALSE. New entry events shall be ignored while ItemTrackingActive is TRUE. ResetButton shall clear the alarm, set ItemTrackingActive and the warning to FALSE, and reset the timer without requiring any additional sensor condition. ResetButton shall have priority over EntrySensor and ExitSensor events in the same scan. When SystemEnable is FALSE, ConveyorOutput and ItemTrackingActive shall be FALSE and active tracking shall be cancelled, but a latched JamAlarm shall remain unchanged.

title: Three-Station Conveyor Congestion and Jam Detection
requirement: Design an LD program that monitors material congestion at three consecutive conveyor stations. The BOOL inputs Station1Occupied, Station2Occupied, and Station3Occupied indicate whether material is present at each station. When the BOOL input SystemEnable is TRUE and no jam emergency stop is latched, the BOOL output ConveyorOutput shall be TRUE. If either Station1Occupied and Station2Occupied are simultaneously TRUE, or Station2Occupied and Station3Occupied are simultaneously TRUE, and this adjacent congestion condition remains continuously TRUE for two seconds, the BOOL output CongestionWarning shall become TRUE. CongestionWarning shall immediately become FALSE when neither adjacent pair remains simultaneously occupied. If all three station inputs remain continuously TRUE for three seconds, the BOOL output JamEmergencyStop shall become TRUE and remain latched, and ConveyorOutput shall immediately become FALSE. After JamEmergencyStop is latched, removing the material shall not automatically restart the conveyor. To permit reset, all three station inputs must first remain continuously FALSE for at least two seconds. After this clear condition has been satisfied, ResetButton = TRUE shall clear JamEmergencyStop and CongestionWarning. If SystemEnable remains TRUE, ConveyorOutput shall then resume. A ResetButton command before the two-second all-clear condition is satisfied shall be ignored.

title: Four-Pump Runtime-Balancing Rotation Control
requirement: Design an LD program that controls four equivalent water pumps and balances their accumulated operating time. The retained DINT outputs Pump1Runtime, Pump2Runtime, Pump3Runtime, and Pump4Runtime shall store the accumulated one-second runtime counts of their corresponding pumps. When RunDemand becomes TRUE, the controller shall select one healthy pump with the smallest accumulated runtime. If several healthy pumps have the same minimum runtime, the lowest-numbered pump shall be selected. Pump1Output, Pump2Output, Pump3Output, and Pump4Output shall indicate which corresponding pump is selected and running; exactly the selected pump output shall be TRUE. The selected pump shall continue running until RunDemand becomes FALSE or that pump develops a fault. On each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of OneSecondPulse, only the runtime output of the running pump shall increase by one. If the running pump develops a fault while RunDemand is TRUE, it shall stop immediately and the healthy pump with the smallest accumulated runtime shall be selected. A pump whose fault clears shall become eligible for a later selection but shall not replace a healthy pump that is already running. If all four pumps are faulted while RunDemand is TRUE, all pump outputs shall be FALSE and NoPumpAvailableAlarm shall be TRUE. When a healthy pump becomes available again, it shall be selected automatically and the alarm shall clear. No fixed-time rotation during a continuous run is required, and no more than one pump output may be TRUE.

title: Three-Compressor Staged Pressure Control with Fault Substitution
requirement: Design an LD program that controls three air compressors according to tank pressure and substitutes healthy compressors for faulted units. Compressor1Output, Compressor2Output, and Compressor3Output shall be the run outputs for Compressor1, Compressor2, and Compressor3 respectively. When SystemEnable is FALSE, all three compressor outputs, RequiredCompressorCount, and CapacityInsufficientAlarm shall be zero or FALSE. When SystemEnable is TRUE, RequiredCompressorCount shall be determined directly from TankPressure: 0 compressors when TankPressure is greater than or equal to 7.0 bar, 1 compressor when TankPressure is greater than or equal to 5.0 bar but lower than 7.0 bar, 2 compressors when TankPressure is greater than or equal to 4.0 bar but lower than 5.0 bar, and 3 compressors when TankPressure is lower than 4.0 bar. No pressure-delay timers or retained pressure stages are required. The controller shall set TRUE the number of healthy compressor outputs specified by RequiredCompressorCount, using the fixed priority Compressor1Output, Compressor2Output, then Compressor3Output. A faulted compressor shall not run. If fewer healthy compressors are available than RequiredCompressorCount, all healthy compressor outputs shall be TRUE and CapacityInsufficientAlarm shall be TRUE. The alarm shall otherwise be FALSE.
input_constraints: TankPressure >= 0.0.

title: Dual-LED Alternating Flash with Mode Selection
requirement: Design an LD program that controls two LEDs in two selectable flashing modes. CurrentMode shall use 0 = Normal and 1 = Fast. Each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of ModeButton shall toggle CurrentMode between Normal and Fast. Holding ModeButton TRUE shall not cause repeated changes. While SystemEnable is TRUE, the LEDs shall alternate, beginning with LedAOutput TRUE and LedBOutput FALSE. In Normal mode, the active LED shall change every one second. In Fast mode, it shall change every 500 milliseconds. When the mode changes, the flashing phase and timer shall reset and the selected mode shall begin from LedAOutput TRUE. When SystemEnable is FALSE, both LEDs shall be FALSE and the flashing phase shall reset, while CurrentMode shall be retained. ResetButton shall set CurrentMode to Normal, turn both LEDs OFF, and reset all timer and edge-detection states. ResetButton shall have priority.

title: Single-Button Multi-State Dual-LED Control
requirement: Design an LD program that uses one BOOL input ControlButton to control two LEDs and distinguishes short and long presses. LedAOutput shall control LED A and LedBOutput shall control LED B. Outside BlinkMode, a press released before two seconds is a short press and shall advance CurrentState cyclically through State 0 = both LedAOutput and LedBOutput FALSE, State 1 = LedAOutput TRUE and LedBOutput FALSE, State 2 = LedAOutput FALSE and LedBOutput TRUE, State 3 = both outputs TRUE, and then back to State 0. If ControlButton remains TRUE for two seconds, the press is a long press and shall toggle BlinkMode. When BlinkMode is entered, CurrentState shall become 0 and both LED outputs shall begin flashing together, starting TRUE for 500 milliseconds and then FALSE for 500 milliseconds. Short presses shall be ignored while BlinkMode is TRUE. A long press while BlinkMode is TRUE shall exit BlinkMode and return to State 0. Each physical press shall cause at most one operation; releasing the button after a long press shall not generate a short press. ResetButton shall immediately exit BlinkMode, set CurrentState to 0, set both LED outputs FALSE, and reset all timers and button states.

title: Two-Liquid Proportional Filling and Mixing Control
requirement: Design an LD program that mixes two liquids in a fixed 3:2 volume ratio. Each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of FlowPulseA represents 10 L of Liquid A, and each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of FlowPulseB represents 10 L of Liquid B. Each batch requires 60 L of Liquid A and 40 L of Liquid B, corresponding to 6 pulses of FlowPulseA and 4 pulses of FlowPulseB. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of StartButton shall start a new batch only when the system is idle and has been reset. At batch start, LiquidACount and LiquidBCount shall be 0 and both ValveAOutput and ValveBOutput shall become TRUE. While ValveAOutput is TRUE, each rising edge of FlowPulseA shall increment LiquidACount by one. When LiquidACount reaches 6, ValveAOutput shall immediately become FALSE and LiquidACount shall remain at 6. While ValveBOutput is TRUE, each rising edge of FlowPulseB shall increment LiquidBCount by one. When LiquidBCount reaches 4, ValveBOutput shall immediately become FALSE and LiquidBCount shall remain at 4. Holding either flow pulse continuously TRUE shall not cause repeated counting. If one liquid reaches its target before the other, only its corresponding valve shall close while the other valve remains open. When both LiquidACount = 6 and LiquidBCount = 4, both valves shall be FALSE and MixerOutput shall become TRUE. MixerOutput shall remain TRUE for two seconds. After two seconds, MixerOutput shall become FALSE and BatchCompletePulse shall become TRUE for one PLC scan. After batch completion, the system shall remain stopped and a new StartButton command shall be ignored until ResetButton becomes TRUE. ResetButton shall immediately close both valves, stop the mixer, clear both counts, clear all batch states and timers, and force BatchCompletePulse FALSE. ResetButton shall have priority over StartButton and all other operations.

title: Dual-Contactor Safe Switching with Feedback Interlock
requirement: Design an LD program that safely controls two mutually exclusive contactors. If only SelectA is TRUE, ContactorA is requested; if only SelectB is TRUE, ContactorB is requested. If both selections are FALSE, both outputs shall be FALSE. If both selections are TRUE, both outputs shall be FALSE and SelectionConflictAlarm shall be TRUE. When changing from one running contactor to the other, the running output shall turn OFF immediately and both outputs shall remain OFF for a fixed two-second switching delay. Selection changes during this delay shall not restart the timer. At the end of the delay, the controller shall evaluate the current selection and start a contactor only if exactly one valid selection is present. ContactorAOutput and ContactorBOutput shall never both be TRUE. If ContactorAFeedback and ContactorBFeedback are simultaneously TRUE, FeedbackFaultAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched, and both outputs shall be FALSE. No individual one-second feedback-confirmation timer is required. ResetButton shall clear FeedbackFaultAlarm only when both feedback inputs are FALSE. While FeedbackFaultAlarm is latched, neither contactor may run.

title: Four-Motor Exclusive Selection with Fault Interlock
requirement: Design an LD program that controls four motors from four BOOL selection inputs. SelectMotor1 through SelectMotor4 correspond respectively to Motor1Output through Motor4Output. A valid command exists only when exactly one selection input is TRUE. If exactly one healthy motor is selected, only its corresponding Motor1Output, Motor2Output, Motor3Output, or Motor4Output shall be TRUE immediately and all other motor outputs shall be FALSE. If all selections are FALSE, all motor outputs shall be FALSE. If two or more selections are TRUE, all motor outputs shall be FALSE and SelectionConflictAlarm shall be TRUE. Each motor has an independent fault input. If the uniquely selected motor is faulted, no motor shall run and SelectedMotorFaultAlarm shall be TRUE. The controller shall not automatically substitute a different motor. Both alarms shall clear automatically when their current input conditions are no longer present. No retained motor state or switching-delay timer is required.

title: Dust-Concentration-Based Fan Speed Control with Hysteresis
requirement: Design an LD program that automatically controls the speed of a dust-extraction fan according to the REAL input DustConcentration in mg/m3. The REAL output FanSpeedCommand shall range from 0.0 to 100.0 percent. When SystemEnable is TRUE and the system is not in HighDustMode, the fan speed shall be determined as follows: if DustConcentration <= 20.0 mg/m3, FanSpeedCommand = 0.0%; if 20.0 < DustConcentration < 70.0 mg/m3, FanSpeedCommand = (DustConcentration - 20.0) * 2.0; and if DustConcentration >= 70.0 mg/m3, FanSpeedCommand = 100.0%. When DustConcentration reaches or exceeds 80.0 mg/m3, the controller shall enter and retain HighDustMode. While HighDustMode is TRUE, FanSpeedCommand shall be forced to 100.0% and HighDustAlarm shall be TRUE regardless of the normal proportional-speed calculation. HighDustMode shall remain active while DustConcentration is greater than or equal to 60.0 mg/m3. It shall clear only when DustConcentration becomes strictly less than 60.0 mg/m3. After HighDustMode clears, FanSpeedCommand shall immediately return to the normal speed calculation based on the current DustConcentration. When SystemEnable is FALSE, FanSpeedCommand shall be 0.0%, HighDustMode shall be FALSE, and HighDustAlarm shall be FALSE.
input_constraints: 0.0 <= DustConcentration <= 100.0

title: Single-Lane Underground Car Park Passage Control
requirement: Design an LD program to control a single-lane passage between the ground floor and the basement of an underground car park. GroundEntryPulse indicates that a vehicle from the ground floor has entered the passage. BasementEntryPulse indicates that a vehicle from the basement has entered the passage. GroundExitPulse indicates that a vehicle traveling from the basement has completely exited the passage at the ground floor. BasementExitPulse indicates that a vehicle traveling from the ground floor has completely exited the passage at the basement. GroundGreenLight and GroundRedLight control the ground-floor entrance lights, and BasementGreenLight and BasementRedLight control the basement entrance lights. When the passage is idle, GroundGreenLight and BasementGreenLight shall be TRUE and GroundRedLight and BasementRedLight shall be FALSE. If GroundEntryPulse occurs while the passage is idle, the controller shall enter the GroundToBasement state. Both green-light outputs shall immediately become FALSE and both red-light outputs shall become TRUE. This state shall remain active until BasementExitPulse occurs. If BasementEntryPulse occurs while the passage is idle, the controller shall enter the BasementToGround state and keep both red-light outputs TRUE until GroundExitPulse occurs. While a vehicle occupies the passage, entry events from either direction shall not change the active direction or release the passage. An exit event that does not correspond to the active direction shall also be ignored. If GroundEntryPulse and BasementEntryPulse occur simultaneously while the passage is idle, neither vehicle shall be admitted, the passage shall remain idle, and DirectionConflictAlarm shall be TRUE for that scan. The DINT output PassageState shall be 0 in Idle, 1 in GroundToBasement, and 2 in BasementToGround. ResetButton shall immediately return the controller to the idle state, clear DirectionConflictAlarm, set both green-light outputs TRUE, and set both red-light outputs FALSE. ResetButton shall have priority over all vehicle events.
input_constraints: GroundEntryPulse, BasementEntryPulse, GroundExitPulse, and BasementExitPulse are one-scan event signals.

title: Manual and Automatic Pick-and-Place Control
requirement: Design an LD program for a pick-and-place system that transfers a product from Conveyor A to Conveyor B. The system supports mutually interlocked manual and automatic operation. ManualMode is a BOOL level input. When ManualMode is TRUE and no automatic cycle is active, ManualClipButton closes the gripper, ManualTransferButton commands the transfer mechanism, and ManualReleaseButton opens the gripper and runs Conveyor B to release and remove the product. Manual command inputs are assumed not to be pressed simultaneously. When ManualMode is FALSE, a one-scan AutoStartPulse shall start one automatic cycle only if ProductPresent is TRUE and no automatic cycle is already active. The automatic sequence consists of three phases. First, in the Clipping phase, GripperClosedOutput shall be TRUE until ClipCompletePulse occurs. Second, after ClipCompletePulse, the controller shall enter the Transferring phase. GripperClosedOutput shall remain TRUE and TransferOutput shall remain TRUE for two seconds. At the end of two seconds, the controller shall enter the Releasing phase, set GripperClosedOutput FALSE, set TransferOutput FALSE, and set ConveyorBOutput TRUE. ConveyorBOutput shall remain TRUE until ReleaseCompletePulse occurs. After ReleaseCompletePulse, the automatic cycle shall end and all automatic outputs shall be FALSE. The DINT output AutoPhase shall be 0 in Idle, 1 in Clipping, 2 in Transferring, and 3 in Releasing. The BOOL output AutoCycleActive shall be TRUE exactly while AutoPhase is 1, 2, or 3 and FALSE while AutoPhase is 0. A new automatic cycle may then be started by another AutoStartPulse. AutoStartPulse shall be ignored while an automatic cycle is already active or while ManualMode is TRUE. Manual commands shall be ignored while an automatic cycle is active, even if ManualMode changes to TRUE during that cycle. ResetButton shall immediately abort any automatic cycle, stop all actuators, clear the automatic state and transfer timer, and clear any retained manual gripper state. ResetButton shall have highest priority.
input_constraints: AutoStartPulse, ClipCompletePulse, and ReleaseCompletePulse are one-scan event signals.
ManualClipButton, ManualTransferButton, and ManualReleaseButton are assumed not to be TRUE simultaneously.

title: Redundant Boiler Pressure Protection with Sensor Disagreement Detection
requirement: Design an LD program that protects a boiler using two redundant REAL pressure sensors, Pressure1 and Pressure2, measured in bar. When SystemEnable is TRUE, FuelValveOutput shall be TRUE exactly when no protection alarm is latched, both pressure values are below 10.0 bar, and ABS(Pressure1 - Pressure2) is less than or equal to 0.5 bar; it shall be FALSE otherwise. If Pressure1 >= 10.0 bar or Pressure2 >= 10.0 bar, FuelValveOutput shall immediately become FALSE and OverpressureTrip shall become TRUE and remain latched. If ABS(Pressure1 - Pressure2) > 0.5 bar, FuelValveOutput shall immediately become FALSE and SensorDisagreementAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. Clearing the pressure condition or restoring agreement between the sensors shall not automatically clear either latched alarm. When ResetButton is TRUE, Pressure1 < 8.0 bar, Pressure2 < 8.0 bar, and ABS(Pressure1 - Pressure2) <= 0.5 bar, both alarms shall be cleared. If these reset conditions are not satisfied, ResetButton shall have no effect on the latched alarms. When SystemEnable is FALSE, FuelValveOutput shall be FALSE while any previously latched alarms shall remain unchanged. After a valid reset, if SystemEnable is TRUE and all normal operating conditions are satisfied, FuelValveOutput shall immediately become TRUE.
input_constraints: Pressure1 >= 0.0.
Pressure2 >= 0.0.

title: Three-Machine Production Cycle Synchronization
requirement: Design an LD program that coordinates three machines in the same production cycle and verifies that their completion times differ by less than 50 milliseconds. CycleStartPulse is a one-scan event that starts a new cycle only when no cycle is active and no synchronization fault is latched. At cycle start, Machine1Run, Machine2Run, and Machine3Run shall all become TRUE. Machine1DonePulse, Machine2DonePulse, and Machine3DonePulse are one-scan completion events. When a machine produces its completion pulse during an active cycle, its corresponding Run output shall immediately become FALSE and that machine shall be recorded as completed for the current cycle. The first valid machine completion shall start a 50 ms synchronization window. If all three machines complete while the elapsed time from the first completion is strictly less than 50 ms, the cycle shall successfully complete, all three Run outputs shall be FALSE, CycleActive shall become FALSE, and CycleCompletePulse shall be TRUE for one PLC scan. If 50 ms elapses from the first completion before all three machines have completed, the cycle shall fail: all three Run outputs shall become FALSE, CycleActive shall become FALSE, and SyncFaultAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. A completion occurring at exactly 50 ms after the first completion is not considered synchronized because the required deviation is strictly less than 50 ms. Done pulses received while no cycle is active shall be ignored. A new CycleStartPulse received while a cycle is already active shall be ignored. While SyncFaultAlarm is latched, CycleStartPulse shall be ignored. ResetButton shall immediately abort any active cycle, clear all per-cycle completion states and synchronization timing, clear SyncFaultAlarm, and force all three Run outputs and CycleCompletePulse FALSE. ResetButton shall have highest priority.
input_constraints: CycleStartPulse, Machine1DonePulse, Machine2DonePulse, and Machine3DonePulse are one-scan event signals.

title: Winding Machine Turn Count with Two-Stage Speed Control
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a winding machine according to TargetTurns. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of StartButton shall start a winding cycle when the controller is idle, TargetTurns is greater than 0, and WireBreakFault is FALSE. At cycle start, CurrentTurns shall reset to 0. Each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of TurnPulse while the machine is running shall increase CurrentTurns by one. When more than three turns remain, MotorRun and HighSpeedOutput shall be TRUE. When one to three turns remain, MotorRun and LowSpeedOutput shall be TRUE. HighSpeedOutput and LowSpeedOutput shall never be TRUE at the same time. PauseButton shall temporarily set all motor outputs to FALSE while retaining the active cycle and CurrentTurns; winding shall resume automatically when PauseButton becomes FALSE. When CurrentTurns reaches TargetTurns, all motor outputs shall become FALSE and WindingCompletePulse shall be TRUE for one scan. If WireBreakFault becomes TRUE during a cycle, the cycle shall be cancelled immediately and all motor outputs shall become FALSE. WindingFaultAlarm shall directly follow WireBreakFault and shall not be latched. Clearing the fault shall not resume the cancelled cycle; a new StartButton transition is required. ResetButton shall cancel any cycle and reset CurrentTurns to 0.
input_constraints: TargetTurns >= 0.

title: Ordered Material Sequence Detection with Fault Lockout
requirement: Design an LD program that verifies that three materials arrive in the fixed order A, then B, then C before processing is permitted. MaterialAPulse, MaterialBPulse, and MaterialCPulse are one-scan event signals. The controller shall initially wait for Material A. If MaterialAPulse occurs alone, the controller shall advance to waiting for Material B. While waiting for Material B, MaterialBPulse occurring alone shall advance the controller to waiting for Material C. While waiting for Material C, MaterialCPulse occurring alone shall complete the required sequence. After the valid A-B-C sequence is completed, ProcessEnable and SequenceComplete shall become TRUE and remain TRUE until ResetButton is activated. If an unexpected material pulse occurs at any stage, SequenceFaultAlarm shall immediately become TRUE and remain latched. Specifically, Material B or C is invalid while waiting for A; Material A or C is invalid while waiting for B; and Material A or B is invalid while waiting for C. If two or more material pulses are TRUE in the same PLC scan before sequence completion, the event shall also be treated as a sequence fault. After SequenceFaultAlarm is latched, all subsequent material pulses shall be ignored and ProcessEnable shall remain FALSE until ResetButton is activated. After sequence completion, all subsequent material pulses shall also be ignored until ResetButton. The DINT output CurrentStep shall be 0 while waiting for A, 1 while waiting for B, 2 while waiting for C, 3 after successful completion, and 4 after a sequence fault. ResetButton shall clear the current sequence state, SequenceComplete, SequenceFaultAlarm, and ProcessEnable and return the controller to waiting for Material A. ResetButton shall have highest priority.
input_constraints: MaterialAPulse, MaterialBPulse, and MaterialCPulse are one-scan event signals.

title: Timed Forward-Pause-Reverse Mixer Control with Emergency Stop
requirement: Design an LD program that executes an automatic mixer sequence consisting of three seconds of forward rotation, one second of stopped pause, and three seconds of reverse rotation. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of StartButton shall start a new cycle only when the controller is idle, EmergencyStop is FALSE, and EmergencyStopAlarm is FALSE. During the first phase, ForwardOutput shall be TRUE and ReverseOutput shall be FALSE for exactly three seconds. After three seconds, both outputs shall become FALSE and the controller shall enter a one-second pause phase. After the one-second pause, ReverseOutput shall become TRUE and ForwardOutput shall remain FALSE for exactly three seconds. At the end of the reverse phase, both rotation outputs shall become FALSE, the cycle shall end, and CycleCompletePulse shall become TRUE for one PLC scan. ForwardOutput and ReverseOutput shall never be TRUE simultaneously. The DINT output CurrentPhase shall be 0 in Idle, 1 in Forward, 2 in Pause, 3 in Reverse, and 4 while an emergency-stop fault is latched. The BOOL output CycleActive shall be TRUE exactly while CurrentPhase is 1, 2, or 3 and FALSE while CurrentPhase is 0 or 4. StartButton commands received while a cycle is active shall be ignored. If EmergencyStop becomes TRUE during any phase, both rotation outputs shall immediately become FALSE, the current cycle shall be aborted, all phase timing shall be reset, and EmergencyStopAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. Clearing EmergencyStop shall not automatically resume or restart the aborted cycle. While EmergencyStopAlarm is latched, StartButton shall be ignored. When ResetButton is TRUE and EmergencyStop is FALSE, ResetButton shall clear EmergencyStopAlarm and return the controller to Idle. If EmergencyStop remains TRUE, ResetButton shall not clear the alarm. EmergencyStop shall have priority over ResetButton, and ResetButton shall have priority over StartButton.

title: Three-Floor Elevator Single-Request Control
requirement: Design an LD program for a simplified three-floor elevator that processes one cabin request at a time. CabinFloor1, CabinFloor2, and CabinFloor3 are one-scan request inputs. A request shall be accepted only when the controller is idle, the door is fully closed, and exactly one cabin request is TRUE. The requested floor shall be retained until it is reached. New requests shall be ignored while a request is active. Elevator position is indicated by the mutually exclusive inputs AtFloor1, AtFloor2, and AtFloor3. If the requested floor is above the current floor, MotorUpOutput shall be TRUE; if it is below, MotorDownOutput shall be TRUE. When the requested floor sensor becomes TRUE, both motor outputs shall stop and DoorOpenOutput shall remain TRUE until DoorOpenLimit becomes TRUE. The door shall then remain open for three seconds with both door-motion outputs FALSE. After three seconds, DoorCloseOutput shall remain TRUE until DoorClosedLimit becomes TRUE, after which the controller shall return to idle. A request for the current floor shall begin the door-opening sequence without moving the elevator. The DINT output CurrentDirection shall be 0 while stopped, 1 while moving upward, and 2 while moving downward. The DINT output ControllerState shall be 0 in Idle, 1 in MovingUp, 2 in MovingDown, 3 in OpeningDoor, 4 in DoorHold, 5 in ClosingDoor, and 6 while EmergencyStopAlarm is latched. The two motor outputs shall never be TRUE together, the two door-motion outputs shall never be TRUE together, and movement is permitted only while DoorClosedLimit is TRUE. EmergencyStop shall immediately stop all outputs, abort the active request, set CurrentDirection to 0 and ControllerState to 6, and latch EmergencyStopAlarm. When ResetButton is TRUE and EmergencyStop is FALSE, ResetButton shall clear the alarm and return the controller to idle. If ResetButton is TRUE while EmergencyStop is TRUE, the reset command shall have no effect.
input_constraints: CabinFloor1, CabinFloor2, and CabinFloor3 are one-scan event signals.
AtFloor1, AtFloor2, and AtFloor3 are mutually exclusive.
DoorOpenLimit and DoorClosedLimit shall not be TRUE simultaneously.

outputs.name: ControllerState
