outputs.constraint: 0 = Idle, 1 = MovingUp, 2 = MovingDown, 3 = OpeningDoor, 4 = DoorOpenHold, 5 = ClosingDoor, 6 = EmergencyStopFault

title: Intersection Traffic Light Control with Day and Night Modes
requirement: Design an LD program to control a two-direction road intersection with North-South (NS) and East-West (EW) traffic lights. The controller has SystemEnable and NightMode inputs. When SystemEnable is TRUE and NightMode is FALSE, the intersection shall operate in a repeating daytime sequence consisting of six phases: NS green for 1 second, NS yellow for 500 milliseconds, all red for 200 milliseconds, EW green for 1 second, EW yellow for 500 milliseconds, and all red for 200 milliseconds before repeating from NS green. During NS green, NSGreen shall be TRUE and EWRed shall be TRUE. During NS yellow, NSYellow shall be TRUE and EWRed shall remain TRUE. During the first all-red phase, NSRed and EWRed shall both be TRUE. During EW green, EWGreen shall be TRUE and NSRed shall be TRUE. During EW yellow, EWYellow shall be TRUE and NSRed shall remain TRUE. During the second all-red phase, NSRed and EWRed shall both be TRUE. NSGreen and EWGreen shall never be TRUE simultaneously. The DINT output ControllerMode shall be 0 when disabled, 1 in daytime mode, and 2 in night mode. In daytime mode, the DINT output DayPhase shall be 0 for NS green, 1 for NS yellow, 2 for the first all-red phase, 3 for EW green, 4 for EW yellow, and 5 for the second all-red phase. DayPhase shall be 0 whenever ControllerMode is 0 or 2. When NightMode becomes TRUE while SystemEnable is TRUE, the current daytime phase and its timer shall be discarded immediately and the controller shall enter night mode. In night mode, all red and green outputs shall be FALSE and NSYellow and EWYellow shall flash synchronously: both yellow lights shall be TRUE for 500 ms and then FALSE for 500 ms, repeating continuously. Night mode shall always begin with the yellow lights ON. When NightMode changes from TRUE to FALSE while SystemEnable remains TRUE, the night flashing state shall be discarded and a new daytime sequence shall begin immediately from the NS-green phase. When SystemEnable is FALSE, all six traffic-light outputs shall be FALSE and all daytime and nighttime timing states shall be reset. When SystemEnable becomes TRUE again, the controller shall start from NS green if NightMode is FALSE or from the yellow-ON phase if NightMode is TRUE.

outputs.name: DayPhase
outputs.constraint: 0 = NSGreen, 1 = NSYellow, 2 = AllRedAfterNS, 3 = EWGreen, 4 = EWYellow, 5 = AllRedAfterEW

title: Variable-Frequency Drive Speed Control with Soft Ramp
requirement: Design an LD program that controls a variable-frequency drive using a 4-20 mA analog speed-reference signal. The REAL input SpeedCurrent represents the analog current in mA and shall be linearly mapped from 4.0-20.0 mA to a target frequency of 0.0-50.0 Hz. Therefore, 4.0 mA corresponds to 0.0 Hz and 20.0 mA corresponds to 50.0 Hz. When RunCommand is FALSE, DriveRunOutput shall be FALSE, FrequencyCommand shall immediately become 0.0 Hz, and all ramp timing state shall be reset. When RunCommand becomes TRUE, DriveRunOutput shall become TRUE and FrequencyCommand shall move toward TargetFrequency using a soft ramp instead of changing immediately. When TargetFrequency - FrequencyCommand is greater than or equal to 10.0 Hz, FrequencyCommand shall increase by exactly 10.0 Hz at each completed one-second interval. If the target frequency decreases while the drive remains running and FrequencyCommand - TargetFrequency is greater than or equal to 10.0 Hz, FrequencyCommand shall decrease by exactly 10.0 Hz at each completed one-second interval. If the difference between FrequencyCommand and TargetFrequency is less than 10.0 Hz, the next ramp update shall set FrequencyCommand exactly to TargetFrequency without overshoot. Changes in SpeedCurrent while running shall immediately update TargetFrequency, but FrequencyCommand shall continue following the new target through the same bidirectional ramp. FrequencyCommand shall always remain within 0.0-50.0 Hz. A new ramp interval shall begin after each frequency update.
input_constraints: 4.0 <= SpeedCurrent <= 20.0

title: RFID-Based Material Storage Allocation
requirement: Design an LD program that automatically assigns incoming materials to compatible empty storage slots according to an RFID-identified material type. The system contains six storage slots. MaterialType = 1 represents Type A, MaterialType = 2 represents Type B, and MaterialType = 3 represents Type C. Type A materials may be stored only in Slot1 or Slot2, Type B materials only in Slot3 or Slot4, and Type C materials only in Slot5 or Slot6. RFIDValidPulse is a one-scan event indicating that a new material type has been identified. When RFIDValidPulse occurs and no assignment is currently active, the controller shall select the lowest-numbered compatible slot whose corresponding SlotOccupied input is FALSE. If a compatible empty slot is found, AssignedSlot shall be set to that slot number and AssignmentValid shall become TRUE. The assignment shall remain latched until StorageCompletePulse occurs or ResetButton is activated. While AssignmentValid is TRUE, all new RFIDValidPulse events shall be ignored. When StorageCompletePulse occurs during an active assignment, the assignment shall be cleared, AssignedSlot shall return to 0, and AssignmentValid shall become FALSE so that a new material can be processed. StorageCompletePulse received when no assignment is active shall be ignored. The controller shall not directly modify or internally assume the occupied state of any storage slot; Slot1Occupied through Slot6Occupied are external physical-status inputs. If RFIDValidPulse occurs for a valid MaterialType but all compatible slots are occupied, no assignment shall be made, AssignedSlot shall remain 0, and NoAvailableSlotAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. If RFIDValidPulse occurs with MaterialType outside the range 1 to 3, no assignment shall be made and InvalidMaterialAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. While either alarm is latched, new RFID allocation requests shall be ignored. ResetButton shall clear any active assignment, AssignedSlot, NoAvailableSlotAlarm, and InvalidMaterialAlarm, but shall not change any SlotOccupied input state. ResetButton shall have highest priority.
input_constraints: RFIDValidPulse and StorageCompletePulse are one-scan event signals.
MaterialType values 1, 2, and 3 represent valid material types A, B, and C respectively.

outputs.name: AssignedSlot
outputs.constraint: 0 = no active assignment, 1 to 6 = assigned storage slot

title: Automatic Car Wash Sequence Control
requirement: Design an LD program for a single-station automatic car wash. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of StartButton shall start a wash cycle only when VehiclePresent is TRUE, the controller is idle, EmergencyStop is FALSE, and EmergencyStopAlarm is FALSE. The wash cycle shall contain three sequential phases: spraying for 1 second, brushing for 2 seconds, and drying for 1 second. During the Spray phase, SprayOutput shall be TRUE and BrushOutput and DryerOutput shall be FALSE. After 1 second, the controller shall enter the Brush phase, in which BrushOutput shall be TRUE and the other two process outputs shall be FALSE. After 2 seconds, the controller shall enter the Dry phase, in which DryerOutput shall be TRUE and the other two process outputs shall be FALSE. After 1 second of drying, all process outputs shall become FALSE, the cycle shall end, and CycleCompletePulse shall be TRUE for one PLC scan. The DINT output CurrentPhase shall be 0 in Idle, 1 in Spray, 2 in Brush, 3 in Dry, and 4 while an emergency-stop fault is latched. The BOOL output CycleActive shall be TRUE exactly while CurrentPhase is 1, 2, or 3 and FALSE while CurrentPhase is 0 or 4. After a cycle has started, changes in VehiclePresent shall not interrupt the current cycle. Additional StartButton commands during an active cycle shall be ignored. If EmergencyStop becomes TRUE during any phase, all process outputs shall immediately become FALSE, the cycle shall be aborted, all phase timers shall be reset, CurrentPhase shall become 4, CycleActive shall become FALSE, and EmergencyStopAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. Clearing EmergencyStop shall not automatically resume or restart the aborted cycle. When ResetButton is TRUE and EmergencyStop is FALSE, ResetButton shall clear EmergencyStopAlarm and return the controller to Idle. EmergencyStop shall have highest priority.

title: Automatic Filling and Capping Production Line
requirement: Design an LD program for an automatic single-bottle filling and capping production line. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of StartButton shall enable automatic operation when no fault is latched. In the WaitingForBottle state, ConveyorOutput shall be TRUE. When BottleAtFillStation becomes TRUE, ConveyorOutput shall immediately become FALSE and the controller shall enter the Filling state. In the Filling state, FillValveOutput shall be TRUE until FillLevelReached becomes TRUE. The controller shall then close the filling valve, mark the current bottle as filled, and restart the conveyor to move the bottle toward the capping station. When BottleAtCapStation becomes TRUE after the current bottle has been successfully filled, ConveyorOutput shall become FALSE and CapperOutput shall become TRUE. CapperOutput shall remain TRUE until CapCompletePulse occurs. After capping is complete, CapperOutput shall become FALSE, the filled status for the current bottle shall be cleared, ConveyorOutput shall become TRUE, and the controller shall return to WaitingForBottle for the next bottle. If BottleAtCapStation becomes TRUE before the current bottle has completed the Filling state, the line shall immediately stop, FaultAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched, and all actuator outputs shall become FALSE. The DINT output CurrentState shall be 0 in Idle, 1 in WaitingForBottle, 2 in Filling, 3 while conveying a filled bottle toward the capping station, 4 in Capping, and 5 in Fault. The BOOL output CycleActive shall be TRUE exactly while CurrentState is 1, 2, 3, or 4 and FALSE while CurrentState is 0 or 5. StartButton commands shall be ignored while the automatic sequence is already active. EmergencyStop shall immediately stop all actuator outputs, abort the current bottle sequence, set CurrentState to 5 and CycleActive to FALSE, and latch FaultAlarm TRUE. Clearing EmergencyStop shall not automatically restart the line. When ResetButton is TRUE and EmergencyStop is FALSE, ResetButton shall clear FaultAlarm and all retained bottle-processing states. If ResetButton is TRUE while EmergencyStop is TRUE, the reset command shall have no effect. After reset, CurrentState shall be 0, CycleActive shall be FALSE, and a new StartButton rising edge shall be required to restart the production line.
input_constraints: CapCompletePulse is a one-scan event signal.

outputs.name: CurrentState
outputs.constraint: 0 = Idle, 1 = WaitingForBottle, 2 = Filling, 3 = MovingToCap, 4 = Capping, 5 = Fault

title: Textile Machine with Thread-Break and Material-Empty Protection
requirement: Design an LD program for a textile machine with normal start-stop control, thread-break protection, and automatic stopping when input material is unavailable. A FALSE-to-TRUE transition of StartButton shall start the machine only when ThreadPresent = TRUE, MaterialPresent = TRUE, ThreadBreakAlarm = FALSE, and MaterialEmptyAlarm = FALSE. While running, MachineRun shall remain TRUE until StopButton is activated or a fault occurs. If ThreadPresent becomes FALSE while MachineRun is TRUE, MachineRun shall immediately become FALSE and ThreadBreakAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. If MaterialPresent becomes FALSE while MachineRun is TRUE, MachineRun shall immediately become FALSE and MaterialEmptyAlarm shall become TRUE and remain latched. If both conditions become FALSE in the same scan while the machine is running, both alarms shall latch TRUE. Restoring ThreadPresent or MaterialPresent shall not automatically clear the corresponding alarm and shall not automatically restart the machine. StopButton shall stop the machine normally without setting either alarm. When ResetButton is TRUE, ThreadPresent = TRUE, and MaterialPresent = TRUE, ResetButton shall clear both alarms. A valid reset shall leave MachineRun FALSE, so a new StartButton rising edge is required to restart the machine. If the reset conditions are not satisfied, ResetButton shall have no effect on the latched alarms. The BOOL output ReadyToRestart shall be TRUE exactly when MachineRun = FALSE, ThreadPresent = TRUE, MaterialPresent = TRUE, ThreadBreakAlarm = FALSE, and MaterialEmptyAlarm = FALSE; it shall be FALSE otherwise. Fault conditions shall have priority over StartButton and normal running logic.

title: Two-Product Vending Machine Transaction Control
requirement: Design an LD program for a simplified automatic vending machine with two products. Product1 costs 150 cents and Product2 costs 250 cents. The machine accepts 50-cent, 100-cent, and 200-cent coin events through Coin50Pulse, Coin100Pulse, and Coin200Pulse. Each coin input is a one-scan pulse. The inserted amount shall be accumulated in the retained output Balance. SelectProduct1Pulse and SelectProduct2Pulse are one-scan selection events. When Product1 is selected, the controller shall first check Product1Available. If the product is unavailable, no product shall be dispensed, the balance shall remain unchanged, and SoldOut indication shall be TRUE for that scan. If Product1 is available but Balance is less than 150 cents, no product shall be dispensed, the balance shall remain unchanged, and InsufficientBalance shall be TRUE for that scan. If Product1 is available and Balance is at least 150 cents, DispenseProduct1Pulse shall be TRUE for one scan, ChangeAmount shall equal Balance minus 150, ChangeValidPulse shall be TRUE for one scan, and Balance shall be reset to 0. Product2 shall follow the same logic using a price of 250 cents and Product2Available: a successful Product2 purchase shall set DispenseProduct2Pulse TRUE for one scan, set ChangeAmount to Balance minus 250, set ChangeValidPulse TRUE for one scan, and reset Balance to 0. Failed purchase attempts shall never reduce the accumulated balance. ChangeAmount shall be 0 whenever ChangeValidPulse is FALSE. ResetButton shall have highest priority and shall immediately clear Balance and all transaction-result outputs without dispensing a product.
input_constraints: Coin50Pulse, Coin100Pulse, Coin200Pulse, SelectProduct1Pulse, and SelectProduct2Pulse are one-scan event signals.
At most one of Coin50Pulse, Coin100Pulse, Coin200Pulse, SelectProduct1Pulse, and SelectProduct2Pulse is TRUE in any PLC scan.

title: Three-Stage Settling Tank Pump-Valve Interlock Control
requirement: Design an LD program for a simplified three-stage wastewater settling system consisting of Tank1, Tank2, and Tank3 connected in series. Each tank provides mutually exclusive processed high-level and low-level status inputs. If both level inputs of a tank are FALSE, its level is considered to be between the low and high thresholds. The BOOL output SystemActive shall always equal SystemEnable. When SystemEnable is TRUE, transfer from Tank1 to Tank2 shall start when Tank1HighLevel is TRUE and Tank2HighLevel is FALSE. Pump12 and Valve12 shall operate together and remain active after transfer starts until Tank1LowLevel becomes TRUE or Tank2HighLevel becomes TRUE. Tank2HighLevel shall therefore immediately block or stop transfer from Tank1. Transfer from Tank2 to Tank3 shall follow the same logic: Pump23 and Valve23 shall start when Tank2HighLevel is TRUE and Tank3HighLevel is FALSE, remain active through the intermediate-level region, and stop when Tank2LowLevel becomes TRUE or Tank3HighLevel becomes TRUE. Tank3 shall discharge through OutletPump and OutletValve. Discharge shall start when Tank3HighLevel becomes TRUE and shall remain active until Tank3LowLevel becomes TRUE. Each pump and its corresponding valve shall always have identical operating states. OverflowAlarm shall be TRUE whenever Tank1HighLevel and Tank2HighLevel are both TRUE, or whenever Tank2HighLevel and Tank3HighLevel are both TRUE. OverflowAlarm shall not be latched and shall clear automatically when neither blocking condition is present. When SystemEnable is FALSE, all pumps and valves shall immediately turn OFF, all retained transfer states shall be reset, SystemActive shall be FALSE, and OverflowAlarm shall be FALSE. When SystemEnable becomes TRUE again, transfer decisions shall be made from the current level inputs rather than restoring any previous transfer state.
input_constraints: Tank1HighLevel and Tank1LowLevel shall not both be TRUE in the same scan.
Tank2HighLevel and Tank2LowLevel shall not both be TRUE in the same scan.
Tank3HighLevel and Tank3LowLevel shall not both be TRUE in the same scan.
For each tank, HighLevel = FALSE and LowLevel = FALSE represents a level between the two thresholds.

title: Dual-Controller Hot-Standby Failover Control
requirement: Design an LD program for a simplified dual-controller hot-standby system. The system contains a primary controller and a backup controller. When SystemEnable is TRUE and the system is initialized with PrimaryHealthy = TRUE, the primary controller shall be active and the backup controller shall remain inactive. PrimaryActive and BackupActive shall never be TRUE simultaneously. While the primary controller is active, if PrimaryHealthy becomes FALSE and BackupHealthy is TRUE, an 80 ms failover confirmation timer shall start. The primary controller shall remain active during the confirmation interval. If PrimaryHealthy remains FALSE continuously for 80 ms, PrimaryActive shall become FALSE, BackupActive shall become TRUE, and FailoverActive shall become TRUE. If PrimaryHealthy becomes TRUE before the 80 ms interval is completed, the failover timer shall reset and the primary controller shall remain active. Once the backup controller becomes active, recovery of PrimaryHealthy shall not automatically switch control back to the primary controller. The backup controller shall remain active until a valid ResetButton command or SystemEnable becomes FALSE. Once FailoverActive becomes TRUE, it shall remain TRUE even if the backup controller later becomes unhealthy, and it shall be cleared only by a valid ResetButton command or by SystemEnable becoming FALSE. If PrimaryActive is TRUE and both PrimaryHealthy and BackupHealthy are FALSE, both active outputs shall immediately become FALSE and NoControllerAlarm shall become TRUE without waiting for the failover timer. If BackupActive is TRUE and BackupHealthy becomes FALSE, both active outputs shall immediately become FALSE and NoControllerAlarm shall become TRUE. NoControllerAlarm shall remain latched until a valid reset or system disable. ResetButton shall reinitialize the system to the primary controller only when PrimaryHealthy is TRUE. A valid reset shall set PrimaryActive = TRUE, BackupActive = FALSE, FailoverActive = FALSE, and NoControllerAlarm = FALSE. If PrimaryHealthy is FALSE, ResetButton shall have no effect. When SystemEnable is FALSE, both controllers shall be inactive, FailoverActive and NoControllerAlarm shall be FALSE, and the failover timer and retained controller state shall be reset.

title: Three-Zone Zero-Pressure Accumulation Conveyor
requirement: Design an LD program for a three-zone accumulation conveyor arranged as Zone1 -> Zone2 -> Zone3 -> Exit. Each zone has one occupancy sensor. When SystemEnable is TRUE, Zone1Motor shall be TRUE exactly when Zone1Occupied is TRUE and Zone2Occupied is FALSE. Zone2Motor shall be TRUE exactly when Zone2Occupied is TRUE and Zone3Occupied is FALSE. Zone3Motor shall be TRUE exactly when Zone3Occupied is TRUE and ExitAvailable is TRUE. If the downstream destination of a zone becomes unavailable, the corresponding zone motor shall stop immediately. Multiple non-conflicting zones shall run simultaneously whenever their individual operating conditions are satisfied. When SystemEnable is FALSE, all three motors shall be OFF.

title: Fair Arbitration for Two Conveyor Merge Lines
requirement: Design an LD program to arbitrate transfers from two feeder conveyors, Line A and Line B, into one main conveyor. RequestA and RequestB indicate pending transfer requests. A new transfer may be granted only when MainLineAvailable is TRUE and no transfer is active. If only one line requests transfer, that line shall be granted. If both lines request simultaneously, the line that was not served most recently shall receive priority. Once a line is granted, the grant shall remain active until TransferCompletePulse occurs. New requests shall not change the active grant. After completion, the completed line shall be recorded as the most recently served line. During the scan in which TransferCompletePulse completes an active transfer, GrantA, GrantB, and MergeBusy shall all become FALSE; pending requests shall not be evaluated for a new grant until the following PLC scan. GrantA and GrantB shall never both be TRUE. The BOOL output MergeBusy shall be TRUE exactly when GrantA or GrantB is TRUE and shall be FALSE otherwise. ResetButton shall cancel any active transfer and initialize the arbitration so that Line A receives priority on the first simultaneous request.
input_constraints: TransferCompletePulse is a one-scan event signal.

title: Two-Hand Safety Start with Synchronization Window
requirement: Design an LD program for a simplified two-hand machine-start control. The BOOL output Armed shall initially be TRUE when both buttons are released. When MachineReady is TRUE and Armed is TRUE, pressing either LeftButton or RightButton shall set Armed FALSE, start a 500 ms synchronization window, and set the BOOL output SyncWindowActive TRUE. The second button must become TRUE before the 500 ms window expires. If both buttons are TRUE within the valid window, PressEnable shall become TRUE and SyncWindowActive shall become FALSE. If the window reaches 500 ms before the second button becomes TRUE, SyncWindowActive shall become FALSE and PressEnable shall remain FALSE. PressEnable shall remain TRUE only while both buttons remain pressed and MachineReady remains TRUE. Releasing either button or losing MachineReady shall immediately set PressEnable to FALSE. After a successful activation or an expired synchronization attempt, Armed shall remain FALSE until both buttons have been released; it shall then become TRUE again. ResetButton shall immediately disable PressEnable, set SyncWindowActive FALSE, and require both buttons to be released before Armed becomes TRUE again.

title: Motor Start Feedback Monitoring and Failure Protection
requirement: Design an LD program for a motor with command-to-feedback supervision. StartPulse is a one-scan command that starts the motor when no alarm is active. After a valid start, MotorCommand shall become TRUE and the controller shall wait for MotorRunningFeedback. The feedback must become TRUE within 2 seconds. If the feedback becomes TRUE before the timeout, the controller shall enter the Running state. If MotorRunningFeedback is still FALSE when the 2-second startup interval expires, MotorCommand shall become FALSE and StartFailureAlarm shall latch TRUE. While the motor is running, loss of MotorRunningFeedback shall immediately set MotorCommand to FALSE and latch FeedbackLostAlarm. StopButton shall stop the motor normally without generating an alarm. ResetButton shall clear both alarms only when MotorRunningFeedback is FALSE. Reset shall not automatically restart the motor.
input_constraints: StartPulse is a one-scan event signal.

title: Three-Type Product Routing with Destination Blocking
requirement: Design an LD program for a simplified product-sorting conveyor. ProductDetectedPulse indicates the arrival of one new product, and ProductType identifies the product as Type 1, Type 2, or Type 3. Type 1 shall be routed to Lane1 using Diverter1, Type 2 shall be routed to Lane2 using Diverter2, and Type 3 shall be routed to Lane3 using Diverter3. When a new product is accepted, ProductType shall be latched as CurrentRoute and shall not change until sorting is complete, even if the external ProductType input changes. Only one product may be processed at a time, and new ProductDetectedPulse events shall be ignored while ProcessingActive is TRUE. If the lane corresponding to CurrentRoute is available, MainConveyor and only the corresponding Diverter1, Diverter2, or Diverter3 output shall operate. If the required destination lane is unavailable, MainConveyor and all three diverter outputs shall stop and RouteBlocked shall become TRUE. The product shall not be rerouted to another lane. When the required lane becomes available again, routing shall resume automatically. SortCompletePulse shall clear the current route and return the controller to idle. ResetButton shall cancel the active routing operation.
input_constraints: ProductDetectedPulse and SortCompletePulse are one-scan event signals.
ProductType is 1, 2, or 3 whenever ProductDetectedPulse is TRUE.

title: Two-Station Pallet Transfer Handshake Control
requirement: Design an LD program for pallet transfer from Station A to Station B. TransferRequestPulse is a one-scan request from the source station. A TransferRequestPulse shall be accepted when SourcePalletPresent is TRUE, DestinationReady is TRUE, DestinationPalletPresent is FALSE, and no transfer is already active; it shall be rejected otherwise. When a valid request is accepted, TransferAcceptedPulse shall be TRUE for one scan, TransferBusy shall become TRUE, and TransferConveyor shall run. The accepted transfer shall remain active even after TransferRequestPulse returns to FALSE. While TransferBusy is TRUE, new requests shall be ignored. The transfer shall be considered successfully completed only when TransferCompletePulse occurs in a scan in which DestinationPalletPresent is TRUE. A TransferCompletePulse received while DestinationPalletPresent is FALSE shall be ignored and the transfer shall remain active. On successful completion, TransferConveyor and TransferBusy shall become FALSE and TransferFinishedPulse shall be TRUE for one scan. ResetButton shall immediately cancel any active transfer and return the controller to idle.
input_constraints: TransferRequestPulse and TransferCompletePulse are one-scan event signals.

title: Two-Level Parking Retrieval Sequence Control
requirement: Design an LD program for a simplified two-level automated parking system with five parking platforms. The upper level contains Slot1, Slot2, and Slot3 from left to right. The lower level initially contains Slot4 under Slot1, Slot5 under Slot2, and an empty position under Slot3. Only retrieval of upper-level vehicles in Slot1, Slot2, and Slot3 is considered. RetrieveRequestPulse is a one-scan event, and SelectedSlot identifies the requested upper parking slot. To retrieve Slot3, no lower platform movement is required and LowerSlot3 shall command Slot3 to move downward directly. To retrieve Slot2, MoveSlot5Right shall first command Slot5 to move one position to the right into the empty lower position under Slot3. After that horizontal movement is confirmed, LowerSlot2 shall command Slot2 to move downward. To retrieve Slot1, MoveSlot5Right shall first command Slot5 to move one position to the right into the empty position under Slot3, MoveSlot4Right shall then command Slot4 to move one position to the right into the position under Slot2, and LowerSlot1 shall finally command Slot1 to move downward. HorizontalMoveCompletePulse confirms completion of the currently commanded lower-platform horizontal movement, and VerticalMoveCompletePulse confirms completion of the currently commanded upper-platform downward movement. Only the completion pulse appropriate for the current step shall advance the sequence; unrelated completion pulses shall be ignored. Once a retrieval sequence begins, SelectedSlot shall be latched and new retrieval requests shall be ignored until the sequence is completed or reset. The DINT output CurrentStep shall be 0 in Idle, 1 while MoveSlot5Right is TRUE, 2 while MoveSlot4Right is TRUE, 3 while LowerSlot1 is TRUE, 4 while LowerSlot2 is TRUE, 5 while LowerSlot3 is TRUE, and 6 in Completed. The BOOL output MovementActive shall be TRUE exactly while CurrentStep is from 1 through 5 and FALSE while CurrentStep is 0 or 6. At most one movement command shall be active at any time. When the downward movement of the selected upper slot is completed, all movement outputs shall turn OFF, CurrentStep shall become 6, MovementActive shall become FALSE, and RetrievalCompletePulse shall be TRUE for one PLC scan. After a completed retrieval, the controller shall remain in the Completed state and shall not accept another retrieval request until ResetButton is activated. ResetButton shall cancel any active sequence, set CurrentStep to 0, clear the selected slot and all movement commands, and restore the controller logic to the standard initial-layout state for the next benchmark test. ResetButton shall have priority over retrieval requests and both completion pulses in the same scan.
input_constraints: RetrieveRequestPulse, HorizontalMoveCompletePulse, and VerticalMoveCompletePulse are one-scan event signals.
SelectedSlot shall be 1, 2, or 3 when RetrieveRequestPulse is TRUE.
Each test starts from the standard physical layout: Slot4 is below Slot1, Slot5 is below Slot2, and the lower position below Slot3 is empty.

The physical parking-platform layout is not continuously simulated after a retrieval. ResetButton restores the benchmark controller to the standard initial-layout state before another retrieval request is accepted.

outputs.name: CurrentStep
outputs.constraint: 0 = Idle, 1 = MoveSlot5Right, 2 = MoveSlot4Right, 3 = LowerSlot1, 4 = LowerSlot2, 5 = LowerSlot3, 6 = Completed
